sections.text: All full-time employees accrue annual leave from their first day of employment at a rate of 1.67 days per completed month of service, for a total of 20 working days per calendar year. Part-time employees accrue annual leave on a pro-rata basis according to their contracted hours. Public holidays are granted separately and do not count against the annual leave balance. Accrued leave is shown in the HR portal and is updated on the last working day of each month.

Employees must submit annual leave requests through the HR portal. Requests for three or fewer consecutive working days require at least 2 business days of notice. Requests for more than three consecutive working days require at least 10 business days of notice. Managers must approve or decline a request within 3 business days of submission. A request that receives no response within that period is escalated automatically to the manager's director. Leave may be declined during documented peak periods, but managers must offer an alternative date range.

Employees may carry over a maximum of 5 unused annual leave days into the next calendar year. Carried-over days must be used by March 31 of the following year, after which they expire without payment. Days above the carryover limit expire on December 31 unless the Head of People approves an exception because business needs prevented the employee from taking leave. Exceptions must be requested in writing before December 1.

sections.section_title: Blackout Periods and Payout on Departure
sections.text: Members of the Finance department may not take annual leave during the final 5 business days of a fiscal quarter without approval from the Finance Director, because those days are reserved for quarter-end close activities. Customer Support team leads coordinate holiday cover so that at least 60 percent of the team is available during the November and December peak season. When employment ends, accrued but unused annual leave for the current year is paid out in the final payroll at the employee's base daily rate. Leave that has already expired under section HR-101.3 is not paid out. Employees who have taken more leave than they accrued at the time of departure will have the excess deducted from their final pay where permitted by local law. Annual leave cannot be used to shorten a contractual notice period without written agreement from the manager.
